claims.text: myasthenia gravis (can precipitate a myasthenic crisis).
claims.quote: Use of magnesium sulfate in patients with underlying myasthenia gravis can precipitate a myasthenic crisis.

claims.text: Mg toxicity: respiratory depression, acute renal failure, rarely pulmonary edema;
claims.quote: Patients receiving Magnesium Sulfate in 5% Dextrose Injection are at risk for magnesium toxicity including respiratory depression, acute renal failure and rarely, pulmonary edema.

claims.text: monitor for facial edema, ↓DTRs and respiratory depression, and check Mg levels during infusion;
claims.quote: Monitor clinical signs of magnesium toxicity (for example, facial edema, diminished strength of deep tendon reflexes, respiratory depression) and magnesium concentrations during infusions

claims.text: DTRs ↓ once Mg > 4 mEq/L and may be absent at 10 mEq/L (respiratory paralysis risk);
claims.quote: The strength of the deep tendon reflexes begins to diminish when serum magnesium concentrations exceed 4 mEq per liter. Reflexes may be absent at concentration of 10 mEq per liter, at which point respiratory paralysis is a potential hazard.

claims.text: keep an injectable calcium salt on hand to counteract it.
claims.quote: an injectable calcium salt should be immediately available to counteract hazards

claims.text: Renal impairment: ↑toxicity risk (Mg is cleared only by the kidneys).
claims.quote: Patients with renal impairment are at greater risk of magnesium toxicity because magnesium is excreted by the body solely by the kidneys
